newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: EU-S.Africa trade talks prolonged.
newsitem.headline: EU-S.Africa trade talks prolonged.

text.p: Talks between South Africa and the European Union to iron out deep-seated differences over a planned trade and development deal will go on a day longer than planned, officials said on Saturday.
Trade analysts took it as a sign that the negotiations, which began in Pretoria on Friday, had hit a rough patch.

Ismail Lagardien, spokesman for South Africa's department of trade and industry, told Reuters that a statement about the outcome of the talks, which would be extended on Sunday, would be issued on Monday.
Both sides said before the start that they were committed to reaching agreement on a package which could reap rich rewards for their export industries.
But negotiators said the weekend talks would probably only be a precursor to further, more detailed negotiations.

The EU first set out its terms for a free trade deal in March, but Pretoria says that proposal does not go far enough in recognising South Africa's development needs and those of the wider southern Africa region.
Plans to exclude 39 percent of farm exports, in order to protect European farmers, have angered the South Africans.

The EU has offered post-apartheid South Africa only partial membership of the Lome Convention, which grants favourable access to EU markets to developing countries elsewhere in Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific.
